schema_name: VSL Estate Intelligence Platform — Schema v2 (proposed)
notes: Extends the LIVE schema in place — no table is dropped or renamed except vsl_flags -> vsl_alerts (kept as a rename+extend, old columns preserved).

History tracking for harvests = vsl_harvests (already append-only, extended). Planting/crop-cycle history = new vsl_parcel_seasons (did not exist — vsl_parcels only held the CURRENT cycle). Activity history = vsl_activities (already append-only, extended). Land-state trend history (soil moisture, weed pressure, etc. changing over time, not just latest value) = new vsl_parcel_land_state_log — this is the gap flagged as 'not sure if that's all the tracking we need'.

Geometry gap: vsl_estate has NO boundary/centroid today. vsl_blocks and vsl_parcels already have geom, both get gps_centroid added. This was the property flagged as discussed-but-dropped from the panel docs (panels list human-facing fields; geometry is map-only, so it never showed up in plot-details.md/block-details.md/estate-details.md, but it's required in the actual table).

Per-activity-type structured properties (18 different field sets in activities.md) are NOT modeled as 18 sparse tables or 100+ mostly-null columns. They go in vsl_activities.activity_properties jsonb, matching the pattern vsl_parcels.agronomy_data already uses live. Shared fields used by every activity (team size, cost, challenges, completion) are typed columns.

All Status/Ratoon/Activities/Alerts/Variety/Harvest/Planting rollup tables in block-details.md and estate-details.md are VIEWS, not stored counter columns, per the earlier drift-risk discussion — listed separately below, not as tables.
Media/Documents/Comments/Infrastructure collapse into 4 polymorphic tables (entity_type + entity_id) instead of 12 near-identical per-level tables, per the schema doc's own suggestion.

SECURITY ADVISORY from Supabase (surfaced, not fixed): public.spatial_ref_sys has Row Level Security disabled. This is a standard PostGIS reference table (not your data), but it is technically exposed to anon/authenticated roles. Remediation SQL is `ALTER TABLE public.spatial_ref_sys ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` — not applied, your call.
Also flagged, not fixed: vsl_estate.nanager_name (typo) and vsl_profiles role check 'MANAGMENT' (typo).

tables.name: vsl_parcel_seasons
tables.description: History of planting cycles per parcel. Today vsl_parcels only stores the CURRENT ratoon_number/planting_date/variety with no history — replanting overwrites the previous cycle with no trace. This table is what makes planting history queryable, and what current_season_id on vsl_parcels points at.

tables.name: vsl_activities
tables.description: Live table only has type/name/status_percent/assigned_to — none of the 18 activity types' specific fields from activities.md have anywhere to live. Extended with the shared execution fields (team size, cost, challenges...) as typed columns and an activity_properties jsonb for the per-type fields (plough depth, chemical type, ridge height, etc.), same pattern as vsl_parcels.agronomy_data.

tables.name: vsl_parcel_soil_tests
tables.description: Lab-tested soil history. Today soil_ph is a single flat value on vsl_blocks only — no per-parcel lab history at all. This is the 'Soil & Land — lab-tested baseline' group from plot-details-v2.md.

tables.name: vsl_parcel_land_state_log
tables.description: Answers the open tracking question: the 'current_*' land-state fields on vsl_parcels (soil moisture, weed pressure, pest pressure, etc.) get overwritten every time a new activity is logged. Without this table you can see the LATEST value but never a trend. One row per change, so analytics can chart e.g. soil moisture or weed pressure over time per parcel.
